--- title: "Homographs" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · LEC_HOMOGRAFOS" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (G · Comprehension; quality class C). Generated on November 28, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea LEC_HOMOGRAFOS`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Homógrafos*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/LEC_HOMOGRAFOS.html). ::: ::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"} **Class C.** It was given to few children, at few time points or in different versions. The task sheet documents the task and its first data; figures are descriptive and cannot yet be used as norms. [What each class means](../../limites.en.qmd#sec-clases). ::: **In one sentence.** Homographs, from age 8 to 11 (1,242 administrations in 3 cohorts). AUC .83–.85 against persistent reading difficulty. ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 10746 | | Battery | — | | Format | forced choice | | Items | 180 | | Task family | G · Comprehension | | Score | Correct responses | | Instructions (platform) | En esta tarea, vas a leer oraciones. Cuando termines de leer una oración, clica sobre ella. *(Spanish)* | ![Example of the screen format (2018 screenshot; not necessarily an item from this task).](../../figuras/pantallas/formato_decision.png){width=45%} ## Theoretical framework In lexical decision the child sees a string of letters and decides whether it is a word ("Is this a word?", YES/NO). It measures **visual word recognition**: fast and secure access to the orthographic lexicon. In 2021/22 it was administered to groups, on tablets, in subtests of 45 stimuli of one to four syllables. Some are biased toward words (36 words and 9 pseudowords) and others toward pseudowords (the reverse proportion). The score is efficiency: correct responses per unit of time. **What the evidence says:** - **Children decide by searching their lexicon, not by reading to themselves.** Beginning and advanced readers show length effects, but their orthographic neighborhood effects resemble those of adults and do not change when articulation is blocked. They base the decision on a lexical search [@vandenboer2012lexical]. - **In Spanish, the orthographic lexicon carries weight beyond decoding.** In 1,070 schoolchildren from Grade 2 to Grade 6, lexical orthographic processing contributed to reading competence and became more refined with years of practice [@cuadro2014lexico]. - **The proportion of words and pseudowords shifts the response criterion.** Participants adopt a single criterion that depends on the set of stimuli, not on each trial [@paul1992criterio]. That proportion changes both accuracy and response times [@ratcliff2004diffusion]. With 80% words, a child who always answers "YES" gets 80% right: sensitivity and bias should be separated. - **Group screening on tablets is feasible.** A tablet application given to 616 five-year-olds predicted Grade 1 reading difficulties with a sensitivity of 90% [@zugarramurdi2022lexiland]. **What our data show.** There is one administration per child and school year: there is no stability estimate and no α. - **Validity.** It is the family with the best concurrent validity on the platform. Against persistent difficulty, AUC from .75 to .87 between ages 9 and 11. Against low Woodcock-Muñoz fluency in the same school year, AUC from .66 to .81 (ρ = .30–.58). - **Bias and length.** The versions biased toward words and toward pseudowords perform almost the same. The one-syllable versions, given only at ages 6–7, are the weakest (AUC .56–.74). - **Homographs.** AUC .84–.85 against persistent difficulty and ρ = .59–.69 with Woodcock-Muñoz, the highest relation in the group. Given the instructions, it seems to measure silent sentence reading efficiency more than comprehension of homographs. - **Caution.** At ages 6–7 efficiency is very skewed (extreme values up to 172), and at age 11 the reference group is small (80–102 children). ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 9.2| 2012| 949|2021/22 | 387| 76| 0| 11| | 10.2| 2011| 948|2021/22 | 428| 0| 327| 15| | 11.2| 2010| 948|2021/22 | 427| 44| 234| 15| | Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness| % floor| % ceiling| |----------:|--:|-------:|-----:|----:|------:|--------:|-------:|---------:| | 9.2| 76| 2012| 19.86| 5.74| 19| -0.31| 0| 0| | 11.2| 44| 2010| 28.75| 7.48| 29| -0.09| 0| 0| **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in correct responses). The usual range goes from P1 to P99 (98% of the children). The minimum–maximum is the one observed after cleaning; the possible range is 0–180 correct responses. | Time point| N|Usual range (P1–P99) |Min.–max. |Possible range | Warning| |----------:|--:|:--------------------|:---------|:--------------|-------:| | 9.2| 76|5.5–30.5 |4–32 |0–180 | | | 11.2| 44|12.3–43.1 |11–44 |0–180 | | ## Reliability There are no two time points with the same children (at least 80). ## Validity **Concurrent.** Outside its domain, the highest relation is with: Word and text reading (9.2, r = .11); Word and text reading (10.2, r = .25); Reading comprehension (11.2, r = .18). **Against reading difficulty and comprehension.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC .83–.85. ![Validity: AUC with 95% confidence interval (labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_LEC_HOMOGRAFOS_F2_validez.png){width=85%} ## Provisional norms | Time point| N| Cohorts| P5| P10| P16| P25| P50| P75| P90| |----------:|---:|-------:|----:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 9.2| 387| 2012| 10.0| 12| 14| 16| 21| 25| 28| | 10.2| 428| 2011| 12.0| 15| 17| 20| 24| 29| 33| | 11.2| 427| 2010| 15.3| 19| 21| 23| 28| 32| 37| These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_LEC_HOMOGRAFOS_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ## Variables that affect it |Variable | Time point| n| Effect| p| |:---------------------------------------|----------:|---:|------:|-----:| |School SES (ρ) | 10.2| 428| 0.028| 0.559| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 10.2| 428| -0.055| 0.569| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 10.2| 426| 0.038| 0.435| |School (ICC) | 10.2| 428| 0.092| | |School SES (ρ) | 11.2| 427| 0.094| 0.052| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 11.2| 426| -0.002| 0.985| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 11.2| 404| -0.073| 0.145| |School (ICC) | 11.2| 427| 0.067| | |School SES (ρ) | 9.2| 171| 0.245| 0.001| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 9.2| 384| 0.103| 0.316| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 9.2| 384| -0.051| 0.320| |School (ICC) | 9.2| 387| 0.028| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Homographs” (code 10746) assesses lexical comprehension of homographs. The child selects a response among the options presented on the screen. It comprises 180 items. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2010, 2011, 2012 and 2013 cohorts it was administered in 4 sessions, from 8 to 11 years of age. The main outcome is the number of correct responses. ## Pending issues - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
